predecessors.note: The page speaks of the time of 'Friesische Freiheit' without a year. Cliopatria rows `frisia` / `magna-frisia` / `frisians` are earlier peoples' rows, not this county. Cliopatria draws the lands inside Holy Roman Empire Minor States from 1260.

A 15 km circle at Esens (7.61E 53.65N). Elevated to a principality in 1654. About 2,500 km2 drawn against the infobox 1,800 km2 of 1800 (the infobox may leave Harlingerland out).

ledger.note: 1 October 1464: the county. 'Emperor Frederick III raised Ulrich to the status of imperial count in 1464'; Ulrich was proclaimed 'Count in Norden, Emden and Emisgonien in East Frisia' on 1 October 1464; the Emperor recognised his rule in Norden on 14 June 1463 (the County of Norden).

region.text: the county of Norden, Emden and Emisgonien in East Frisia

ledger.note: 1539: the seat moves from Emden to Aurich (infobox 'Emden (1464-1539) Aurich (1539-1807)'; the royal-residence entry says Aurich from 1561).
1575: the Jeverland goes to Oldenburg. 'In 1575, East Frisia therefore definitively lost the Jeverland to Oldenburg.' The page does not say when East Frisia held it.

28 January 1600: the Treaty of Berum. 'The lordships of Esens, Stedesdorf and Wittmund were permanently bound to East Frisia by the Treaty of Berum of 1600' (drawn up on 28 January 1600), in personal union and outside the power of the estates.

region.text: the lordships of Esens, Stedesdorf and Wittmund (Harlingerland)

ledger.note: 21 May 1611: the Accord of Osterhusen. 'On 21 May 1611, under heavy pressure from the Dutch, the Accord of Osterhusen was signed by all parties'; Dutch garrisons were stationed in Emden and Leerort and 'would eventually occupy the fortress until 1744'. The page dates the Emden episode from 1595 (the humiliation) and the Agreement of The Hague of 8 April 1603; the garrison year is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the fortresses of Emden and Leerort

ledger.note: 1654: the princes. 'In 1654 the counts of East Frisia, seated at Aurich, were elevated to the rank of princes' (Enno Louis, 'imperial prince' on the County page).
1744: the Dutch occupation of the fortress ends with the Prussian takeover (the page: 'until 1744').

region.text: the fortresses of Emden and Leerort

ledger.note: 25 May 1744: Prussia. 'On 14 March 1744 the Emden Convention was signed to regulate the transition. Charles Edzard's death on 25 May 1744 began the personal union with Prussia'; 'East Frisian independence ended in 1744, when the region was taken over by' Prussia.

certainty.note: The pages give lordships and treaties, not boundaries; the circles are stand-ins calibrated to the 1800 area.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (2 pages; budget 5). New state: Cliopatria has no East Frisia row.

SHAPES. Aurich 7.48E 53.47N 24 km (1,810 km2 against the infobox 1,800 km2 of 1800); Jever 7.90E 53.57N 12 km; Esens 7.61E 53.65N 15 km; Emden 7.20E 53.37N and Leerort 7.45E 53.23N 6 km for the garrisons. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Aurich', 'Emden', 'Jever', 'Esens', 'Leer'. The modern region East Frisia is 3,142 km2 (East Frisia page) which includes Harlingerland and the Jeverland.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The 1464 date is the imperial elevation; Norden was recognised on 14 June 1463. (2) The county's extent before 1575 and when East Frisia held the Jeverland (page: it 'definitively lost' it). (3) The Dutch garrisons: Emden (from 1595 humiliations / the 1603 Hague agreement / 1611 Osterhusen accord) and Leerort; the page says only 'until 1744'. (4) The personal union with Prussia (1744-1807) and the Kingdom of Holland (1806 on the East Frisia page, 9 July 1807 on the County page) are later states' events. (5) The East Frisia page does not give 1464 or 1581; the County page gives 1581 only as Enno III's marriage.
